Where it began

James Douglas Sheahan Neesham, known to everyone as Jimmy, was born in Auckland on 17 September 1990. He started out in first-class cricket with his home province, Auckland.

A move south to Otago before the 2011–12 season suited him well. In one-day games he scored quickly, and with the ball he picked up 5 for 44 against Wellington. It was enough to earn him a place in New Zealand's limited-overs squads for a tour of South Africa.

The player

Few cricketers have made a louder entrance. Batting at number eight on Test debut against India, he made 137 not out, the highest debut score by anyone in that position. In his next Test, against the West Indies in June 2014, he made another hundred. No New Zealander had scored centuries in each of his first two Tests before.

He played 12 Tests in all, between 2014 and 2017. He scored 709 runs at 33.76 with two hundreds and four fifties, took 14 wickets with a best of 3 for 42, and held 12 catches.

What made him special

He was a clean, fearless striker of the ball. Against Sri Lanka in January 2019 he hit five sixes in taking 34 runs from a single over, more than any other New Zealander had managed in a one-day international. He could bowl too, and at the 2019 World Cup he took his first five-wicket haul in ODIs, against Afghanistan.

He also had a knack for being in the middle of big moments. In that World Cup's semi-final he held the catch that took the last Indian wicket. New Zealand finished runners-up at the 2019 World Cup and again at the 2021 T20 World Cup, with Neesham in both squads.

Away from the middle

Few players have packed a bag as often. He turned out for Delhi, Punjab, Mumbai and Rajasthan franchises in the Indian Premier League, for Guyana in the Caribbean, and for Derbyshire and Kent in England. Later came Wellington at home, then sides in Canada, Nepal and Bangladesh. In 2025 he was part of the Fortune Barishal team that won the Bangladesh Premier League.

And finally

Two Test hundreds in his first two matches set a standard that would test anyone. He spent the following years showing he could hit just as hard in the shorter game, on whichever continent his kit happened to land.
